instructions.primary_message: Wash and dry lemons; zest and juice into a medium bowl.
Peel and mince garlic; add to the bowl with the lemon.
Add broth, coconut aminos, and spices to the bowl; whisk to combine the sauce and set aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
355 ml chicken or vegetable broth
½ cup coconut aminos
1 tbsp parsley flakes
¾ tsp black pepper
3 pinch crushed red pepper

instructions.primary_message: Wash zucchini, trim ends, and use a julienne (or regular) peeler to make noodles. Use a paper towel or a clean cloth to squeeze excess moisture out of the zucchini noodles.
Preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels, then cut into 1-inch cubes.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add steak and cook, stirring occasionally, until desired doneness, 5-6 minutes for medium. Transfer to a plate and set aside.
Add sauce to the skillet and whisk. Cook, stirring frequently, until the mixture is reduced by about half, 6-8 minutes.

Stir in butter and, once melted, add zucchini noodles. Cook, stirring constantly, until just tender, 5-6 minutes. Use tongs to remove from skillet and portion onto plates, leaving the excess sauce in the pan.
Return steak to the skillet and toss to coat in the sauce.
To serve, transfer steak to plates with the noodles and top with any remaining sauce. Enjoy!

Wash, dry, and cut cauliflower heads into quarters, then trim off and discard the leaves and thick stem. Using a box grater or food processor, coarsely grate the cauliflower and transfer to a medium bowl. Set aside.
Preheat a large pot over medium-high heat.
While the pot heats up, pat the chicken thighs dry with paper towels and place on a large plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
instructions.secondary_message:
1.36 kg chicken thighs, boneless skinless
¾ tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Once the pot is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Working in batches if necessary, add chicken and sear until golden brown, 2-3 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate and set aside (the chicken will not be cooked all the way through).
Meanwhile, wash, dry, and trim green beans. Transfer to another medium bowl and set aside.
Peel and mince garlic.
Return the pot to medium-high heat. Place garlic, broth, coconut aminos, vinegar, honey, and pepper in the pot; stir to combine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
instructions.secondary_message:
355 ml chicken or vegetable broth
⅓ cup coconut aminos
⅓ cup rice vinegar
2 tbsp honey
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Return chicken to the pot and turn to coat in the sauce. Add green beans, cover, and simmer until chicken is cooked through and green beans are tender-crisp, 10-12 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat another large pot over medium-high heat.
Once the pot is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add cauliflower and season with salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until tender, 8-10 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
¾ tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: To serve, divide cauliflower rice, chicken, green beans, and sauce between plates. Enjoy!
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ½ small bunches asparagus
3 (2 ½ cm) pieces ginger root
6 medium carrots
1 small bunch cilantro
1 lime
1 ½ heads butter (Boston) lettuce

instructions.primary_message: Snap or cut off the woody ends of the asparagus and cut into 1-inch pieces.
In a medium saucepan, bring 1-inch of water to a boil over high heat. Add asparagus and cook, uncovered, until crisp-tender, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince or grate ginger; transfer to a large bowl.
Add coconut aminos, oil, and vinegar to the bowl with the ginger; whisk to combine the dressing.
instructions.secondary_message:
⅓ cup coconut aminos
¼ cup toasted sesame oil
2 tbsp rice vinegar

instructions.primary_message: When the asparagus is done, drain and add to the bowl with the dressing; set aside.
Preheat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or regular skillet over medium-high heat.
While the grill pan heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
instructions.secondary_message:
1.02 kg striploin (New York strip) steak
¾ tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Once the grill pan is hot, coat with oil. Working in batches if necessary, add steak and grill until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate, cover loosely with aluminum foil, and set aside to rest for about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and trim carrots. Using a julienne (or regular) peeler, peel carrots into thin noodle-like sticks; add to bowl with the asparagus.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
Slice lime into wedges.
Thinly slice steak against the grain and add to the bowl with the vegetables. Toss to combine.

Separate the lettuce into leaves. Pile leaves, in stacks of two per wrap, onto plates. Fill with steak, vegetables, and cilantro; sprinkle with sesame seeds. Serve with lime wedges on the side and enjoy!
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
0.68 kg cremini mushrooms
9 baby bok choy
3 (2 ½ cm) pieces ginger root

instructions.primary_message: Thinly slice steak against the grain into strips. Transfer to a medium bowl, add coconut aminos, and toss to combine; set aside to marinate.
instructions.secondary_message:
1.02 kg striploin (New York strip) steak
⅓ cup coconut aminos

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, using a clean cutting board, thinly slice mushrooms; transfer to another medium bowl.
Preheat a large pot over medium-high heat.
Once the pot is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add steak strips to the pot and stir-fry until just cooked through, 6-7 minutes.
Meanwhile, trim ends and separate bok choy into leaves.
When the steak strips are done, transfer to a plate.

Return the pot to medium-high heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add mushrooms and cook, stirring occasionally, until starting to brown, about 5 minutes. (Reserve bowl for the next step.)
While the mushrooms cook, slice white stems of the bok choy crosswise into thin strips; chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces. Transfer leaves to the reserved bowl.
Add bok choy stems to the pot and stir to combine. Cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies are fork-tender, 6-8 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince ginger and garlic; add to the pot and stir-fry until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add bok choy leaves to the pot in handfuls, waiting for the leaves to wilt slightly before adding the next handful.
Return steak strips (and any accumulated juices) to the pot along with coconut aminos and vinegar; stir to combine and remove from heat.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 tbsp coconut aminos
1 tbsp rice vinegar

instructions.primary_message: To serve, divide stir-fry between plates or bowls. Enjoy!
Preheat oven to 220°C (425°F).
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ½ lemons
3 small bunches asparagus
6 caps portobello mushrooms
3 (2 ½ cm) pieces ginger root

instructions.primary_message: Zest and juice lemons into a large bowl.
Peel and mince garlic; add to the bowl with the lemon juice, along with coconut aminos, oil, and spices. Whisk to combine the marinade.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 cloves garlic
3 tbsp coconut aminos
3 tbsp toasted sesame oil
1 ½ tsp oregano, dried
1 ½ tsp salt
¾ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Add steak to the bowl with the marinade, turn to coat, and set aside.
Snap or cut off the woody ends of the asparagus; divide between two baking sheet pans.
Slice mushrooms into ¼-inch thick pieces and add to the baking sheets with the asparagus.
Peel and mince ginger and additional garlic; sprinkle over the veggies.
Drizzle veggies with oil and coconut aminos; sprinkle with sesame seeds, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat and spread out in an even layer.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tbsp toasted sesame oil
2 tbsp coconut aminos
3 tbsp sesame seeds
¾ tsp salt
¾ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Place baking sheets in the oven and roast, tossing once, until veggies are fork-tender, 15-20 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Working in batches if necessary, add the steak and marinade; pan-fry until steak reaches desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate and let rest 5 minutes.
Thinly slice steak against the grain.
To serve, divide veggies and steak between plates. Enjoy!
If using wooden skewers, place 12-18 skewers in a shallow dish of water to soak until you are ready to use them.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 medium zucchini squash
1 ½ small pineapples
1 ½ limes
3 (2 ½ cm) pieces ginger root
1 head butter (Boston) lettuce

instructions.primary_message: Trim zucchini and cut crosswise into 1-inch rounds. Peel, halve, and cut onions lengthwise into 1-inch wide wedges; place both in a large bowl.

Cut off skin from each pineapple, halve, and remove the core. Cut a portion of the pineapple into 12 thin slices to place on top of the burgers; set aside for serving. Large dice remaining pineapples and add to the bowl with the veggies.
Zest limes into the bowl with the veggies and pineapple (set limes aside for later); drizzle with oil, season with salt, and toss to combine.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
1 ½ tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: Thread veggies and pineapple onto skewers and place on a plate; alternatively, you can cook the veggies and pineapple directly on the grill pan. (Reserve the bowl for later use.)
Preheat a grill pan or regular skillet over medium-high heat.

Once the grill pan is hot, working in batches if necessary, place skewers on the grill and cook, turning occasionally, until the veggies are charred and tender, 4-5 minutes. Return to the plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil.
Meanwhile, peel and mince garlic and ginger; add both to the reserved bowl.
Add pork, coconut aminos, salt, and pepper to the bowl with the garlic and ginger; use your hands to thoroughly combine. Form into 6 equal-sized patties and place on a plate.
instructions.secondary_message:
1.02 kg lean ground pork
1 tbsp coconut aminos
¾ tsp salt
¾ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: When the skewers are done, coat the grill with oil. Working in batches if necessary, place burger patties on the grill and cook, undisturbed, for 5 minutes; flip patties, and grill an additional 3-4 minutes, until cooked through. Once done, transfer to a clean plate.
While the burgers are cooking, cut reserved limes into wedges.
Separate the lettuce into leaves and layer one leaf on top of another to create 6 stacks.
To serve, divide lettuce stacks between plates; top with burgers, mayo, and two slices of pineapple. Place skewers on the side, squeeze with lime, and enjoy!
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the mixed greens if they came pre-washed.)
instructions.secondary_message:
3 limes
2 English cucumbers
3 small pkgs grape tomatoes
3 medium carrots
2 small bunches cilantro
1 small pkg fresh mint
1 ½ (142 g) pkg spring mix (mixed greens)

instructions.primary_message: Peel and mince garlic; place in a large bowl.
Juice limes into the bowl with the garlic. Add oil, fish sauce, coconut aminos, sugar, crushed red pepper, and black pepper; whisk to combine the dressing.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 tbsp toasted sesame oil
2 tbsp fish sauce
1 tbsp coconut aminos
1 tbsp brown sugar
¾ tsp crushed red pepper
¾ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Peel, halve, and thinly slice onion into half-moons. Add to the bowl with the dressing, toss to combine, and set aside.
Preheat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or regular skillet over medium-high heat.
While the pan heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate. Season with salt and pepper on both sides.
instructions.secondary_message:
1.02 kg striploin (New York strip) steak
1 ½ tsp salt
1 ½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Once the pan is hot, coat with oil; working in batches if necessary, add steak to the pan and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate and let rest for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, trim and halve cucumbers lengthwise, then thinly slice crosswise into half-moons; halve tomatoes. Add both to the bowl with the dressing.
Peel, trim, and coarsely grate carrots; add to the bowl.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and roughly chop the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Pick mint leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl and set aside.
Right before serving, thinly slice steak against the grain. Add to the bowl with the dressing, along with mixed greens, and toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide salad between plates or bowls and enjoy!
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 limes
9 baby bok choy
3 red bell peppers
0.68 kg cremini mushrooms
1 small bunch cilantro

instructions.primary_message: Peel, halve, and mince onion; peel and mince garlic. Place both in a small bowl.
instructions.secondary_message:
½ medium red onion
3 cloves garlic

instructions.primary_message: Juice limes into the bowl with the onion and garlic; add coconut aminos and almond butter. Whisk to combine the sauce and set aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 tbsp coconut aminos
3 tbsp natural almond butter

instructions.primary_message: Trim bok choy and cut crosswise into 1-inch strips; place in a large bowl.
Trim, seed, and halve bell peppers crosswise, then slice into thin strips; add to the bowl with the bok choy.
Trim and thinly slice mushrooms; add to the bowl and set aside.
Preheat a large pot over medium-high heat.
While the pot heats up, pat steak dry with paper towels, then slice crosswise into thin strips. Season with salt and pepper.
instructions.secondary_message:
1.02 kg striploin (New York strip) steak
¾ tsp salt
¾ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Once the pot is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add steak strips and stir-fry until just cooked through, 4-5 minutes. Using tongs, transfer the steak to a plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil. (Reserve pot with cooking juices for the next step.)
Return the pot to medium-high heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies to the pot and stir-fry until fork-tender, 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, using a clean cutting board, shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.

When the veggies are done, add sauce, steak (and any accumulated juices), and cilantro to the pot; stir to combine. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens and steak is warmed through, 2-3 minutes.
To serve, divide stir-fry and sauce between plates or bowls; top with almonds and enjoy!
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
6 caps portobello mushrooms
3 (2 ½ cm) pieces ginger root
3 medium zucchini squash

instructions.primary_message: Remove stems and scrape out the gills of the mushrooms; small dice, place in a large bowl, and set aside.
Preheat a large pot over medium-high heat.
Once the pot is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add pork, salt, and pepper; cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 5-6 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 tbsp toasted sesame oil
1.02 kg lean ground pork
¾ tsp salt
¾ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, peel and mince ginger and garlic; add both to the bowl with the mushrooms.
When the pork is done, add mushrooms, ginger, and garlic to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies are soft and fragrant, 4-5 minutes.
Add broth and coconut aminos to the pot; stir to combine, cover, and bring the soup to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, reduce heat to medium-low and simmer until flavors blend, about 5 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
2839 ml chicken or vegetable broth
2 tbsp coconut aminos

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, trim zucchini and use a julienne (or regular) peeler to make noodles.
When the soup is done, add zucchini noodles to the pot, stir to combine, and remove from heat.
To serve, divide soup between bowls, drizzle with oil, and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Enjoy!
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tbsp toasted sesame oil
1 tbsp sesame seeds

instructions.primary_message: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ½ medium heads cauliflower
0.68 kg cremini mushrooms
1 small bunch green onions (scallions)
3 (2 ½ cm) pieces ginger root
1 ½ (142 g) pkg baby spinach

instructions.primary_message: Small dice bacon.
Preheat a large pot over medium-high heat.

Once the pot is hot, add bacon and cook, stirring occasionally, until crispy, 5-6 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, remove crispy bacon to a paper towel-lined plate; set aside. (Reserve pot with drippings for later use.)

Using a clean cutting board, cut each cauliflower head into quarters, then trim off and discard the leaves and thick stem. Using a box grater or food processor, coarsely grate the cauliflower and place in a large bowl; set aside.
Thinly slice mushrooms.
Return pot (with drippings) to medium-high heat. Add mushrooms and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 6 minutes.
Meanwhile, trim and cut green onions crosswise into thin pieces. Add half to the bowl with the cauliflower and set the other half aside for garnish.
When the mushrooms are soft, add cauliflower, green onion, and oil to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until cauliflower is soft and beginning to brown, about 6 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince ginger and garlic. Place both in a small bowl along with coconut aminos and maple syrup; whisk to combine the sauce.
instructions.secondary_message:
6 cloves garlic
¼ cup coconut aminos
1 tbsp pure maple syrup

instructions.primary_message: When the cauliflower is done, add spinach to the pot in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Add sauce, stir to combine, and continue to cook until heated through, about 30 seconds. Remove from heat and cover to keep warm.
Preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Working in batches, gently crack eggs into the skillet and cook until the tops of the whites are set but the yolks are still runny, about 4 minutes. Remove from heat and season with salt.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tbsp toasted sesame oil
12 eggs
½ tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: To serve, divide cauliflower rice and eggs between plates. Garnish rice with crispy bacon, reserved green onion, and sesame seeds. Enjoy!
Preheat oven to 230°C (450°F).
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ½ medium heads cauliflower
6 green bell peppers
6 tomatoes
1 small bunch cilantro

instructions.primary_message: Separate each cauliflower into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces. Divide between two large baking sheet pans.
Trim, seed, and medium dice bell peppers. Add to the baking sheets with the cauliflower.
Cut tomatoes into wedges and add to the baking sheets.
Peel, halve, and slice onions lengthwise into ¼-inch thick pieces. Add to the baking sheets.
Drizzle the veggies with oil and coconut aminos, then season with spices. Toss to coat and spread out in an even layer.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
3 tbsp coconut aminos
1 tbsp garlic powder
1 tbsp paprika
¾ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Place baking sheets in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, tossing halfway through, until veggies start to soften, 10-12 minutes.
Meanwhile, shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place in a small bowl, along with yogurt, and stir to combine. Set aside.
Pat steak dry with paper towels and cut into 1-inch pieces. Place in a medium bowl, drizzle with additional coconut aminos and oil, then season with pepper. Toss to coat.
instructions.secondary_message:
1.02 kg striploin (New York strip) steak
3 tbsp coconut aminos
2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: When the veggies are starting to soften, remove from oven. Add steak (and any marinade in the bowl) to the baking sheets, stir to combine, and return to the oven. Continue to bake until veggies are fork-tender and steak is cooked through, 10-12 minutes more. Remove from oven.
To serve, divide steak and veggies between plates; top with cilantro yogurt. Enjoy!
Place butternut squash, broth, coconut milk, paprika, and salt in a large pot. Stir to combine the soup.
instructions.secondary_message:
9 cup frozen butternut squash, pieces
1420 ml chicken or vegetable broth
1 ½ (398 ml) cans coconut milk
1 ½ tsp paprika
¾ tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: Bring the soup to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, reduce heat to low and simmer, stirring occasionally, until squash is very soft, 8-10 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry arugula (skip this step if it came pre-washed). Place in a large bowl.
Add carrots, cranberries, pumpkin seeds, and nutritional yeast to the bowl with the arugula. Set aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ½ (283 g) bags shredded carrots
¾ cup dried cranberries
⅓ cup pumpkin seeds
⅓ cup nutritional yeast flakes

instructions.primary_message: When the soup is done, remove from the heat. Purée soup with an immersion or regular blender (return soup to the pan).
Add vinaigrette to the bowl with the arugula and toss to combine the salad.
Divide soup between bowls and sprinkle with additional pumpkin seeds; serve with salad on the side. Enjoy!
Wash cauliflower and cut off the leaves. Rice (grate) using a hand grater or in a food processor.
Wash carrots and green onions.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 medium carrots
1 ½ small bunch green onions (scallions)

instructions.primary_message: Trim ends, peel, and small dice carrots; transfer to a medium bowl. Trim ends and slice green onions on the diagonal into ⅔ cm pieces; transfer to a small bowl.
Measure out peas and add to bowl with carrots.
Peel and mince garlic. Peel and mince ginger. Transfer both to a small bowl.
instructions.secondary_message:
6 cloves garlic
3 (2 ½ cm) pieces ginger root

instructions.primary_message: Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Cube chicken into bite-sized pieces. Season with salt and freshly ground pepper.
instructions.secondary_message:
1.02 kg chicken breasts, boneless skinless
⅜ tsp salt
⅜ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add chicken and stir-fry until browned, 3-4 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Add more oil to skillet followed by garlic and ginger. Stir fry until fragrant, 15-30 seconds.
Add carrots and peas; stir-fry until tender-crisp, 3-4 minutes.
Add cauliflower rice, mix well, and stir-fry until tender, 2-3 minutes.
In a medium bowl, whisk eggs.
Move all the ingredients to one side of the skillet and pour eggs on the other side. Scramble eggs and mix with everything else.
Return chicken to skillet and add coconut aminos and green onions; stir to combine.
Serve in a bowl and enjoy!
In a small bowl, make a slurry by whisking water with arrowroot until smooth. Add coconut aminos, sesame oil, and red pepper; whisk together. Set aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
6 tbsp cold water
3 tsp arrowroot starch/powder
6 tbsp coconut aminos
3 tsp toasted sesame oil
⅜ tsp crushed red pepper

instructions.primary_message: Wash the fresh produce. Snap (or cut) off woody ends from the asparagus, then cut on an angle into 5 cm pieces; transfer to a large bowl. Seed and cut the bell peppers into 5 cm strips; add to the bowl with asparagus. Trim green onion ends and chop on an angle; transfer to a small bowl.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 small bunches asparagus
3 red bell peppers
1 ½ small bunch green onions (scallions)

instructions.primary_message: Peel and mince or grate the ginger. Peel and mince the garlic. Transfer both to a small bowl.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 (2 ½ cm) pieces ginger root
6 cloves garlic

instructions.primary_message: Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Slice the steak into thin strips.
Add oil to the skillet and swirl to coat bottom. Add the steak strips and cook until browned, 1-2 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate.

Once steak has been transferred, add more oil to the skillet. Add the asparagus, bell pepper, ginger, and garlic. Cook, stirring frequently, until vegetables are crisp-tender and lightly browned, 2-3 minutes.
Return beef to the skillet and add green onions and sauce. Cook until sauce is slightly thickened, 1-2 minutes.
To serve, place stir fry in a bowl and enjoy!

1 ½ medium heads cauliflower
3 medium zucchini squash
2 small bunches green onions (scallions)
3 jalapeño peppers
3 (2 ½ cm) pieces ginger root

instructions.primary_message: Pat the steak dry with paper towels, place on a cutting board, and slice crosswise into thin strips. Place in a medium bowl, add coconut aminos, and stir to coat.
instructions.secondary_message:
1.02 kg flank steaks
3 tbsp coconut aminos

instructions.primary_message: Preheat a large pot over medium-high heat.

Once the pot is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Working in batches if necessary, add steak strips and cook, undisturbed, until browned, about 3 minutes. Turn and continue to cook until desired doneness, 1-2 minutes more. Remove to a plate. (Reserve pot and cooking juices for later use.)

Meanwhile, using a clean cutting board, cut each cauliflower head into quarters; using a box grater, hold the stem end of the cauliflower and coarsely grate. (Alternatively, transfer cauliflower to the bowl of a food processor; pulse until rice-like in consistency.) Place in a large bowl.
Trim and coarsely grate zucchini. Using your hands, gently squeeze to remove excess water, then add to the bowl with the cauliflower.
Trim and cut green onions crosswise into 1-inch pieces. Add to the bowl.

Return the pot (with cooking juices) to medium-high heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add cauliflower, zucchini, green onion, salt, and pepper; cook, stirring occasionally, until cauliflower is soft and starting to brown, 6-7 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tbsp toasted sesame oil
1 ½ tsp salt
¾ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, quarter jalapeño peppers lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon to reduce spice level, then mince. Place in a clean medium bowl. When the cauliflower is done, return steak strips (with any accumulated juices) to the pot. Add the jalapeño mixture and continue to cook, stirring frequently, until warmed through and fragrant, about 1 minute. Remove from heat.

1 small bunch green onions (scallions)

instructions.secondary_message:
1 cup avocado oil mayonnaise

1 tbsp coconut aminos

¼ tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: Thinly slice jalapeño peppers into rings; seed and remove ribs with a spoon to reduce spice level. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Halve and pit avocados; using a spoon, scoop out the flesh and slice crosswise into thin half-moons. Season with salt.
Separate the lettuce into leaves.

In a small bowl mix together chili-garlic sauce, salt, and mayo.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ½ tbsp chili-garlic sauce
3 pinch salt
½ cup mayonnaise

instructions.primary_message: To serve divide egg roll mixture between bowls, top with green onions, sesame seeds, and spicy mayo. Enjoy!
